title: Smart executor: staged contexts, provenance and loop-safety for multi-tool workflows
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: multi-tool chains used by function-calling and structured-output flows have exhibited two classes of failure in production: unbounded recursion/cycles (LLM triggers tool A -> tool B -> tool A) and state pollution from injected tool results. This ticket implements a 'Smart Executor' runtime that enforces staged execution contexts, provenance tagging on tool outputs, and runtime loop-safety with cost-aware pruning. Scope: - Add a lightweight execution context object persisted per-request that records tool call graph IDs, cumulative token cost, and last-seen tool outputs (provenance). - Implement cycle detection using a configurable depth+fingerprint strategy (tool id, arguments fingerprint) and a policy layer (error, truncate, sandbox rerun, or fallback to cached result). - Introduce provenance tags on injected results so LLM prompt construction can selectively include/exclude fields and preserve structured-output schemas. - Support streaming partial tool outputs back through the API with backpressure signals so long-running tools (search, DB queries) can progressively feed the model. - Provide compatibility shims for older SDKs that expect simple linear tool runs: FS to present only final results and to simulate synchronous tool injection. - Add a cost-aware chain pruner that suggests to the LLM or client to short-circuit low-value tool calls when token budget surpasses thresholds. Design decisions: - Use deterministic fingerprinting (sorted args + canonical JSON) for cycle detection to reduce false positives when callers reorder params. - Keep execution context data small and ephemeral; do not persist to disk by default to avoid PI exposure. - Make loop policy configurable per-customer and per-route via route config and account-level defaults. Acceptance criteria: 1) Cycle detection prevents infinite loops in fuzz tests covering 1000 synthetic chains and produces deterministically repeatable traces. 2) Streaming tool outputs are delivered to SDK consumers with <150ms median chunk latency under test harness. 3) Provenance tags are available in the structured output envelope and respected by the prompt-building layer. 4) Compatibility shim returns legacy payloads for SDK v1.x clients without changing host API contract. Non-goals: full debugger UI for call graphs (separate ticket), cross-request persisted tool caches (out of scope).
